claimPolicy.rule: Every material technical claim must state its demonstrated scope and stop where the evidence stops.

proofLevels.name: OBSERVABLE
proofLevels.meaning: A visitor can inspect the implementation or live behavior.

proofLevels.name: ENFORCED
proofLevels.meaning: Executable machinery rejects a prohibited state or operation.

proofLevels.name: TESTED
proofLevels.meaning: Automated qualification or self-tests exercise the mechanism.

proofLevels.name: BENCHMARKED
proofLevels.meaning: Quantitative results exist under a defined protocol.

proofLevels.name: EXTERNALLY_VALIDATED
proofLevels.meaning: Independent customers, evaluators, organizations, or market outcomes provide evidence.

claims.scope: Diamond Gate public product surfaces built with repository-owned HTML, CSS, JavaScript and, where needed, WebGL/WebGL2 and GLSL.
claims.boundary: This does not claim every possible customer project will be framework-free or that native construction automatically guarantees performance.

claims.scope: Registered repository operations executed through the bounded exact-head carrier.
claims.boundary: This is a scoped execution property of admitted repository operations, not a claim that arbitrary software execution is impossible.

claims.scope: Page operations governed by the active Page Excellence toolchain and entry gate.
claims.boundary: A passing gate is evidence that declared qualification conditions passed; it is not a universal guarantee that software contains no defects.

claims.scope: Governed operations whose admission and execution documents bind exact repository state, allowed paths, source identities and digests.
claims.boundary: The claim describes identity and scope enforcement inside this repository lifecycle; it is not a general cryptographic-security claim.

claims.scope: Compilation of a predecessor repository operation into a fresh successor packet when the governing head advances, while preserving declared scope and refusing authority inheritance.
claims.boundary: This is not a general-purpose website compiler and should not be represented as one.

claims.scope: Repository workflows for differential continuity, operation succession, instrument lifecycle, and bounded recovery/requalification.
claims.boundary: This demonstrates repository-level continuity controls; it does not claim uninterrupted service availability under every external failure mode.

claimsNotYetAuthorized: more secure than named third-party policy systems
